channel.title: Pier & Point · Potrero Power Station Block 8
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Potrero Power Station Block 8 (Potrero Power Station), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Potrero Power Station Block 8: The Board's ordinance as enacted on October 13, 2026…
item.description: The Board's ordinance as enacted on October 13, 2026 sets new height limits for Block 8: 133 ft and 93 ft. They take effect 31 days after enactment, November 13, 2026 by our count; until then the earlier limits (125 ft and 85 ft) apply. Source: BOS File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29 (Figure 249.87-2 'Building Heights Maximum') and p. 56 (§5(a): 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment'); Legistar: Final action and Enactment date 10/13/2026, Enactment # 209-26. File 260724 attachment p. 10: 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment.'.
item.source: BOS File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29 (Figure 249.87-2 'Building Heights Maximum') and p. 56 (§5(a): 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment'); Legistar: Final action and Enactment date 10/13/2026, Enactment # 209-26. File 260724 attachment p. 10: 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment.'

item.title: Correction · Potrero Power Station Block 8: The Block 8 page now says a City building permit…
item.description: The Block 8 page now says a City building permit (filed May 19, 2022) lists block 4232, lot 022 and ends its description '(block 8)', so the Chronicle's address is not the only link between the lot and the block. The unit counts now include 348, from the 2024 annual compliance report and the permit's own units field; the permit's description says 342. Source: https://data.sfgov.org/resource/i98e-djp9.json?permit_number=202205194622 ; https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station (2024 Annual Report).

item.title: Correction · Potrero Power Station Block 8: JPMorgan's roughly $200 million of financing for Block…
item.description: JPMorgan's roughly $200 million of financing for Block 8 was announced on August 3, 2026; the date it was agreed is not stated. A 2022 permit application lists an estimated cost of $175 million, which is not a stated development cost. Source: The San Francisco Standard, Aug 3, 2026 (https://sfstandard.com/2026/08/03/jpm-sf-housing-potrero-power-station/); DataSF building permits (https://data.sfgov.org/resource/i98e-djp9.json?permit_number=202205194622); Saitowitz Natoma Architects (https://www.saitowitz.com/potrero-power-block-8).

item.title: Correction · Potrero Power Station Block 8: Block 8's map notes now say Figure 6.2.3 gives it 125…
item.description: Block 8's map notes now say Figure 6.2.3 gives it 125 ft and 85 ft limits and that the '90' MAX' labels are dimension lines, not a 90 ft height. The parcel note no longer says the block has no address: DataSF Parcels lists an active lot at 151 Humboldt St (4232022), the address the Chronicle gives for the building, that lies almost entirely within the footprint (whether to switch the map to it is undecided). The D4D transit facilities are corrected (a shuttle stop and shelter on Block 8; the bus stop and operator restroom are on Block 12), the rental and developer-rename wording is tied to sources, the YA Studio partnership is described as a March 2022 stated intention, and the 2028 completion is shown as a stale phase forecast from SocketSite's October 2020 schedule and SF YIMBY (2021), not a record-based date. The Foster + Partners rendering is no longer hosted here because the sheet is marked (c) Foster + Partners and the state permission page does not cover third-party copying; the Design Review Approval stays linked. Sources and one image label were also corrected. Source: SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final, 2020-02-26 (https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sf.gov/d/acdm-wktn); San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-08-03 (https://www.sfchronicle.com/realestate/article/jpmorgan-housing-san-francisco-22367970.php); SF Planning, Block 8 Design Review Approval, 2022-03-02, and California Barrel Company, 2021 Annual Report, 2022-03 (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station); SocketSite, 2020-10-09 (https://socketsite.com/archives/2020/10/revised-phasing-for-massive-potrero-power-plant-redevelopment.html); SF YIMBY, 2021-03-01 (https://sfyimby.com/2021/03/foster-partners-design-revealed-for-potrero-power-station-hunters-point-san-francisco.html).
item.source: SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final, 2020-02-26 (https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sf.gov/d/acdm-wktn); San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-08-03 (https://www.sfchronicle.com/realestate/article/jpmorgan-housing-san-francisco-22367970.php); SF Planning, Block 8 Design Review Approval, 2022-03-02, and California Barrel Company, 2021 Annual Report, 2022-03 (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station); SocketSite, 2020-10-09 (https://socketsite.com/archives/2020/10/revised-phasing-for-massive-potrero-power-plant-redevelopment.html); SF YIMBY, 2021-03-01 (https://sfyimby.com/2021/03/foster-partners-design-revealed-for-potrero-power-station-hunters-point-san-francisco.html)

item.title: Planned · Potrero Power Station Block 8: JPMorgan Chase's roughly $200 million of… (Aug 3, 2026)
item.description: JPMorgan Chase's roughly $200 million of financing for a 342-unit Foster + Partners-designed building at 151 Humboldt St is announced and reported (SF Standard: 'JPMC's newest commitments were announced Monday', Aug 3, 2026; the Chronicle report carries the same date); neither report gives the date the financing agreement was made (Aug 3, 2026). item.title: Expected · Potrero Power Station Block 8: Completion expected: SocketSite's October 2020… (~2028)
item.description: Completion expected: SocketSite's October 2020 revised-phasing schedule lists Block 8 vertical development 2026-2028 (Phase 1) and SF YIMBY's March 2021 report anticipated completion in 2028; the August 2026 report of JPMorgan financing and a fall 2026 start gives no completion date, and no source since 2021 restates a 2028 completion (~2028). Source: SocketSite, 2020-10-09; SF YIMBY, 2021-03-01; San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-08-03.
item.source: SocketSite, 2020-10-09; SF YIMBY, 2021-03-01; San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-08-03

item.title: Planned · Potrero Power Station Block 8: Planning Director approves the Block 8… (Mar 2, 2022)
item.description: Planning Director approves the Block 8 design review: 14 stories (12 habitable), approximately 125 ft plus rooftop features, 339 units, approximately 18,000 sq ft retail, 166 vehicle spaces; one minor modification to D4D A.8.1 (upper volume 96 ft 8 in deep from Maryland St at levels 9-10 vs 90 ft) (Mar 2, 2022). Source: SF Planning, 2022-03-02.

item.title: Planned · Potrero Power Station Block 8: SF YIMBY reports new design-review… (Mar 1, 2021)
item.description: SF YIMBY reports new design-review applications: Block 8 described as 140 ft with 249 units, six retail spaces, wellness center, pool and an eighth-floor urban farm; the article itself states that Block 8 would begin rising in 2026 and complete in 2028 (Mar 1, 2021). Source: SF YIMBY, 2021-03-01.
